title: Prime coefficients in proper smooth curve families
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $f:C\to S$ a proper smooth morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with nonempty geometrically connected fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] of dimension exactly one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For every prime $\ell$ and every $q\ge0$, the sheaf $R^qf_*\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. No invertibility of $\ell$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0GKV, label lemma-proper-smooth-family-curves; finite-field module form of its constructible abelian conclusion

proof.text: Split S into D(ell) and the closed subscheme defined by the principal ideal (ell). The closed piece has ell = 0 in its global section ring by the ideal-sheaf kernel identity, including nilpotents. The basic-open stalk criterion gives invertibility on the open piece. Noetherian scheme instances supply quasi-compactness and local Noetherianness of both pieces. The source-library open-closed constructibility theorem reduces to these restrictions. Explicitly use LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian for the closed immersion; locally Noetherian open subschemes and the Noetherian-space compactness API supply the open restriction. Immersion finite-type instances supply the closed restriction hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0GKV, cases (a),(b), with source-library open-closed gluing

proof.text: Use the componentwise torsion-ring proper base-change isomorphism supplied by the unit step hasTorsionBaseChange_of_isProper (lemma-weil-pbc-prime-proper-base-change), its exact inverse-image homology comparison, its degree-zero single-object comparison, and preservation of constant sheaves to identify each restriction with the corresponding curve direct image. Smooth geometrically connected fibres imply geometric irreducibility; the fibre dimensions yield smooth relative dimension one, which persists under base change. Smoothness supplies flatness and local finite presentation through their Mathlib instances.

source.place: Tag 0GKV, cases (a),(b), with source-library open-closed gluing

proof.text: On the invertible-prime piece, use finite geometric stalks and the smooth proper specialization theorem. The derived module/abelian comparison gives the required abelian identification; the general specialization comparison transfers its invertibility to bijectivity on module stalks. The finite-stalk specialization criterion supplies finite constant charts. Convert the cover to a locally constant datum and use the trivial stratification.

source.place: Tag 0GKV, cases (a),(b), with source-library open-closed gluing

proof.text: On the characteristic-prime piece, the connected-fibre degree-zero lemma gives constructibility in degree zero. The characteristic-prime high-vanishing lemma gives zero higher direct images in every degree above one; zero sheaves are constructible on the trivial stratification.

source.place: Tag 0GKV, cases (a),(b), with source-library open-closed gluing

proof.text: For degree one on a nonempty characteristic-prime piece, its global sections have characteristic p. The prime-field ring map supplies its scheme structure over the lifted prime field. The Artin-Schreier kernel realization gives a finite locally free module and a Frobenius-semilinear endomorphism whose fixed-point kernel is the underlying abelian higher direct image. The Frobenius vector-bundle theorem makes that kernel constructible. The cyclic-module chart upgrade gives module constructibility. If the base is empty, every sheaf is zero. Transport both piece results along the base-change isomorphisms and apply step one.

Every hypothesis matches. New Step 3: prime proper base change (any base map, f proper) plus the forgetting comparison (3) gives the module exchange over U and Z. Residue fields are unchanged on open and closed subschemes, and nonreduced Z is allowed. New Step 4: U is retrocompact open and Z is its complement, so both are constructible. The assembly node's qcqs and disjoint-cover hypotheses hold, and its conclusion with P = finite locally constant module pullback is exactly the module constructibility definition. Composite pullbacks are made F_ell-linear by naturality of the composition isomorphism together with forgetting (1). Steps 5-9 are unchanged apart from renumbering, and I rechecked their hypotheses: ell invertible on U, a Noetherian base, p=0 on Z, and a semilinear Frobenius F that need not be invertible. I checked empty S/U/Z, nonreduced Z, q=0/1/>=2 and genus 0. The newly declared tool uses (assembly, inverse-image-composition) belong to sk-thm-p1, which the unit cites directly, so they are on-route and acceptable. There is no SGA citation and no route departure. Minor, not faults: the report announces preflight output it does not include, and Step 1 takes relative dimension one from the fibre dimension without spelling out irreducibility of the fibre (a pre-existing step).
